references.text: The same chapter describes how they will flee even when no one pursues them, and their enemies will rule over them.
Isaiah prophesies that they will fall among the captives and under the slain, without strength to rise up against their enemies.
Isaiah describes how Jerusalem stumbled and Judah fell, reflecting the theme of stumbling over one another.
Jeremiah uses similar language about many stumbling and falling over each other.
The prophecy that the arrogant will stumble and fall with no one to raise them up.
Israel could not stand against their enemies because of sin, an example of the fulfillment of this curse.
The book of Judges shows how Israel could not stand against their enemies when the Lord was against them.
Proverbs describes how the wicked flee even when no one pursues.
Deuteronomy contains the same warning about being struck down before your enemies and fleeing in panic.
Moses' song asks how one could chase a thousand if the Lord had not handed them over.
